beliefs.claim: Automated reasoning models exhibit distinct safety failure profiles under adversarial pressure, preventing universal self-correction strategies; this is reinforced by the finding that specific error attribution is highly sensitive to cross-segment dependencies.
beliefs.falsifier: Demonstration of a universal, context-independent error correction algorithm that successfully mitigates failures across heterogeneous tasks without introducing new failure modes.
beliefs.why_retained: New research on dependency-guided failure attribution (DeFA) confirms that reasoning errors are often trace-specific, limiting the efficacy of simple, universal correction mechanisms.

recent_notebooks.summary: Automated reasoning systems struggle with foundational premise validation. Recent integration of causal-guided knowledge editing (CAKE) and failure attribution metrics suggests that explicitly modeling causal dependencies can help identify and rectify foundational errors that adversarial prompts exploit.
recent_notebooks.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits

recent_notebooks.summary: Adapting the CRASH agent framework to diverse industrial domains requires robust failure attribution. By applying causal inference methods to incident reports, agents can map failures back to decisive error steps, improving safety analysis across heterogeneous data environments.
recent_notebooks.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability

recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous agents can better identify metacognitive blind spots by employing failure attribution techniques that isolate the decisive error step in long tool-use trajectories. This allows agents to reconcile expected versus actual outputs effectively.
recent_notebooks.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution
